findings.title: SQL injection allows authentication bypass
findings.evidence: Login with username "admin' -- " and a wrong password returned HTTP 200 (an unknown user returned 401)
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries, hash and compare passwords in application code, and add rate limiting / lockout.

findings.title: Service with known vulnerability (CVE-2011-2523)
findings.evidence: Banner '220 (vsFTPd 2.3.4)' matches CVE-2011-2523: vsFTPd 2.3.4 shipped with a backdoor that opens a shell on port 6200
findings.remediation: Upgrade to a supported, patched version or remove the service. Legacy plaintext protocols such as FTP should be replaced by SFTP/FTPS.

findings.title: Admin interface reachable without authentication
findings.remediation: Require authentication and an admin-role check on every admin route; deny by default.

findings.title: SQL injection (boolean-based)
findings.evidence: Always-true and always-false conditions returned different results (205 vs 99 bytes)

findings.title: SQL injection (error-based)
findings.evidence: A single quote in 'username' triggered a database error: Database error: unrecognized token: "2d711642b726b04401627ca9fbac32f5c8530fb1903cc4db02258717921a488...

findings.title: SQL injection (error-based)
findings.evidence: A single quote triggered a database error: Database error: unrecognized token: "'" Query: SELECT id, name, price FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%laptop'%...
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for every query; never build SQL by string concatenation.

findings.title: Sensitive file publicly accessible
findings.remediation: Remove the file from the web root, deny access to dotfiles and backups at the web server, and rotate any secrets it contained.

findings.title: Sensitive file publicly accessible
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, 74 bytes, first line: -- LabShop backup (fake data)
findings.remediation: Remove the file from the web root, deny access to dotfiles and backups at the web server, and rotate any secrets it contained.

findings.title: Insecure direct object reference exposes user records
findings.evidence: Unauthenticated requests for ids [1, 2, 3] each returned HTTP 200 with id, username, email and role fields
findings.remediation: Require authentication and verify the requesting user owns (or is authorized to view) the record; avoid sequential, guessable identifiers.

findings.title: Reflected cross-site scripting
findings.evidence: Marker markup '<svg onload=labc8c9f0d3>' returned unencoded in the HTML response
findings.remediation: HTML-encode all user-controlled output (context-aware templating) and add a Content-Security-Policy.

findings.title: Verbose database errors disclosed to users
findings.evidence: Response exposed internal details: Database error: unrecognized token: "'" Query: SELECT id, name, price FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%laptop'%'
findings.remediation: Return a generic error page, log details server-side only.

findings.title: Server banner discloses software and version
findings.remediation: Remove version details from the Server header (e.g. ServerTokens Prod) and patch the server.

findings.title: Cookie set without security attributes
findings.remediation: Set HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax (or Strict) on session cookies, and Secure over HTTPS.

findings.title: Missing HTTP security headers
findings.remediation: Add the headers, e.g. Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; X-Frame-Options: DENY; X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; Referrer-Policy: no-referrer.

findings.title: Open TCP port 2121 (unknown)
findings.remediation: Close ports that are not required and restrict the rest with a firewall.

findings.title: Open TCP port 5055 (unknown)
findings.remediation: Close ports that are not required and restrict the rest with a firewall.
